newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish publishers mull new venture with Hachette.
newsitem.headline: Polish publishers mull new venture with Hachette.

text.p: Polish publishers who bid in a consortium with France's Hachette for the Ruch news stand chain are considering cooperating with Hachette on building a new network, the head of the publishers' joint venture said.

The move followed a treasury ministry decision earlier this week to call off earlier talks with the Hachette-led consortium on the sale of Ruch and to once again invite bids for Poland's largest press distribution network.

Maciej Hoffman, president of firm Wydawcy Prasy, said on Friday that it asked Hachette Distribution Services to present a plan of its future presence in Poland and declared it was willing to cooperate in setting up an alternative to Ruch.
"Given Hachette's pledges that it would not abandon the Polish market, we have asked it to present its vision of creating a private press distribution service in Poland," Hoffman said.
The consortium could either form a new firm from scratch, buy an existing firm, or form a joint-venture with a group of existing distributors and that all options were possible.

Late last year, the Hachette-led consortium signed a preliminary agreement with the treasury ministry under which it had exclusive rights to carry out final negotiations on the sale. The ministry is offering 75 percent of Ruch, which has a 65 percent share in the Polish press distribution market and 17,000 kiosks nationwide.
